_comment: 2026 has no official key. Every row was compared with an independent second derivation (blind/2026-Physics/second.json) on 2026-10-30: 7/7 MCQ letters and all 32 written answers agree. Entries below are notes added to the published solution.

adjudications.solutionNote: Note: the susceptibility of a ferromagnetic material also falls as its temperature rises, so option (c) can be argued as printed. The expected answer is paramagnetic because the inverse dependence on temperature (Curie's law, susceptibility proportional to \(\frac{1}{T}\)) is the defining property of paramagnets in the syllabus.
adjudications.why: Both solvers chose B and both flagged that ferromagnets also show it; MEDIUM confidence.
